title: Can I complain if my new home isn't ready when I get the keys?
videoTitle: CAN YOU COMPLAIN ABOUT YOUR NEW HOUSE?
excerpt: A friend collected his keys to find the facilities unfinished. Sean explains the protection homebuyers have under the Housing Development Act, and the tribunal where they can claim without a lawyer.

qa.context: A friend of Sean's paid about RM800,000 for a new home, but at vacant possession the facilities weren't ready and buyers were angry. Many owners don't know what protection they have.
qa.question: What can a buyer do when a new home or its facilities are not delivered as promised?
qa.quote: you need to claim back what is your right
qa.answer: Buyers of residential property are protected by the Housing Development Act, and a developer should hand over only when an architect certifies the facilities are ready. For serious failures you can file a claim at a tribunal without a lawyer, but claim what your SPA promises, not grievances like a cheaper later phase.

reasons.title: Homes have legal protection
reasons.body: The Housing Development Act protects buyers of residential property. Buyers of shop offices or factories are not covered by it.

reasons.title: Facilities should come with the keys
reasons.body: A home without a finished car park or access road can't be lived in, so a developer needs a professional architect's certification before handing over.

reasons.title: Claims don't need a lawyer
reasons.body: The tribunal Sean describes is meant for laymen, and lawyers can't act there. If a developer ignores a reported defect and you pay to fix it, you can claim the cost back.

actions: Read your SPA to know exactly what must be delivered at vacant possession.
Report defects to the developer in writing and keep records and photos.
If they don't respond, fix the defect, keep the bill and claim the cost.
File serious claims at the tribunal yourself rather than hiring a lawyer.
Don't expect a claim to succeed over a later phase being cheaper.
qa.caveat: Minor hairline cracks or patchy paint are not what the tribunal is for. Sean also notes that established developers usually make handover far smoother than small ones.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's English captions for this November 2018 video. The tribunal's name, its filing fee and the deadline for developers to repair are unclear in the captions, so they are left out; check the current tribunal and procedure before filing. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased.
